Finishing services and acceptance points

We support deburring, bead blasting, polishing, anodizing, passivation and plating as appropriate to the selected material. The quotation defines the finish and any accompanying documents; not every treatment is suitable for every alloy.

Deburring and polishing: specify edge breaks, cosmetic faces and any controlled roughness.
Bead blasting: agree appearance, protected interfaces and whether a reference sample is needed.
Anodizing: specify alloy, color, coating requirements and masked threads or mating surfaces.
Passivation and plating: identify the applicable material, process specification, protected areas and acceptance documents.

Critical dimensions are checked at the agreed stage, including after finishing where required. We link the material and treatment documents requested in the order to the relevant part or batch reference.

AI-generated illustrative image. It does not identify alloy grades, stock availability or finish specifications.
Describe the operating conditions

Explain the weight and loading requirements, along with the part's exposure and operating temperature. Describe its electrical behavior and the assembly it mates with. If you have not selected a grade, share these conditions and the applicable specification for engineering review. A catalog category does not establish suitability for a safety-critical application.

Specify the material grade

The catalog groups parts by material: aluminum, stainless steel, copper and brass, and engineering plastics. Each group covers different grades. State the grade and condition your design requires, then confirm whether alternatives are permitted and which material documents you need.

Material examples named in the original brochure
Aluminum: 6061, 7075 and 2024.
Stainless steel: 304, 316 and 17-4PH.
Copper and brass: printed as C3600 and H62 in the source brochure.
Engineering plastics: POM, PEEK and PPSU.
Other named materials: titanium, Inconel, Kovar and Invar.

This list preserves examples from the source brochure; it does not confirm current stock or availability. Confirm the exact alloy designation, grade, condition, process suitability and material documents for each part. In particular, verify the intended C3600 designation before quoting.

Compare material families by the job
Family	Examples in the brochure	Compare and confirm
Aluminum	6061, 7075, 2024	Compare strength/stiffness, part mass, environment and finish needs. Confirm exact alloy/temper, alternatives, finish compatibility and documents.
Stainless steel	304, 316, 17-4PH	Compare environment, mechanical requirements and condition. Confirm grade, heat treatment where applicable, finish, standard and certificates.
Copper / brass	C3600, H62 as printed	Compare electrical or thermal role and service environment. Confirm the alloy designation and material documents. Check the brochure's C3600 reference with us before ordering.
Engineering plastics	POM, PEEK, PPSU	Compare temperature, load, chemical exposure, electrical behavior and mating material. Confirm exact grade, operating conditions and traceability documents.

These are comparison prompts, not a material recommendation. Properties vary by grade, condition and design; confirm the requirements with the drawing and applicable specification.

How should I compare material options?

A material family alone is not a purchase specification. Compare named grades using the conditions above, then record the grade, condition and applicable standard. If a substitute is proposed, approve it explicitly and confirm the available material documents.

Define the finish requirements

Specify visual appearance separately from the finish's function. Name the required finish standard and revision where applicable, and describe color, gloss, texture, coating thickness or roughness only where these are controlled requirements. Mark masked areas, cosmetic faces and surfaces for corrosion protection, electrical contact or sealing. Confirm process suitability, availability and required documentation for the selected material and part.

A photograph shows surface appearance but cannot establish coating thickness or surface roughness. It cannot verify process compliance either, so a reference image alone is not a finish specification.

AI-generated illustration. The pictured finishes are not LZZ samples and do not identify a coating, roughness value or process standard.
Resolve dimensions after treatment

Tell the supplier whether acceptance dimensions apply before or after finishing. Highlight mating bores, threads and other interfaces where a coating matters. Specify edge breaks and cosmetic faces separately so functional and appearance criteria can be reviewed together.

Record the requirements in your RFQ

Put the agreed material and finish requirements on the controlled drawing or specification. Include inspection and traceability needs in your RFQ package, using the quality checklist to check the details before you prepare an inquiry.
